Described as a thin 115-pound woman in her early 50s carrying only a folding toothbrush; offered up to five meals a day; accepted no rides from San Francisco. Has spoken to church women's and student groups for 15 years; close to the Quakers.

route_planned: Third petition (Peace Department) to be presented to the President on arrival in Washington
notable_details: Photo of her walking in front of a Whittier building. Continuation prints the full text of the petition for a Peace Department and Secretary of Peace; asks readers to mail signed copies to Peace Pilgrim Cologne NJ.

notable_details: In San Diego she did one TV and four radio programmes and spoke at a high school. Story went out over AP UP and INS. Described as a voluntary worker for the American section of WILPF.
date_note: Undated; written from California in late January 1953 (after Tijuana). British spelling suggests the London paper Peace News.

route_before: Walked all the way from California; worn out two pairs of shoes

miles_reported: 1,900 since Jan 1 (3,344,000 steps); 25 mi/day at 4 mph
route_before: Los Angeles - San Diego - Phoenix - Tucson - El Paso - Fort Worth - Dallas - Oklahoma City
route_planned: Chicago then Washington DC and New York City; expects the trip to take a year
people_mentioned: Jim Jackson (reporter)
notable_details: Arrived in Oklahoma City on a Thursday and is stopping temporarily. Has worn out two pairs of shoes and is well into a third. Carries no money; her only luggage is in a tunic pocket (three petitions and copies of her message). Turns down rides by pointing to her tunic.
date_note: Undated; a Thursday in about May 1953.

route_before: Starting in Los Angeles January 1; walked across the desert many times all night
route_planned: To the President and the United Nations
notable_details: Walked into the city last week. Tells of a night in the desert when a rough-looking man invited her into his parked car to get warm; he later admitted he had meant to attack her but could not. Says she has slept and eaten better in Texas and Oklahoma than anywhere. Calls Oklahoma City the greatest spiritual center she has found.
date_note: Undated; about a week after the Oklahoma City arrival.

miles_reported: 5,000 (planned); three pairs of shoes worn out
route_before: Left LA in January after viewing the Tournament of Roses Parade; San Diego - Phoenix - El Paso - Dallas - Oklahoma City - Topeka - Kansas City - St. Louis
route_planned: Chicago; Washington (Department of Peace plea to Eisenhower); New York City (United Nations)
notable_details: Explained her message here yesterday. Ending (cut off) says she became interested in helping others while working with a Quaker society in Philadelphia. Same headline as row 035 (St. Louis): probably the St. Louis story or a reprint of it.
date_note: Undated; after St. Louis and before Chicago (about July 1953). Index label Ag is unexplained.

route_before: Started LA January 1; letters received from Benson AZ and Deming NM; in Tucson the weekend of March 1; now reported in Texas
people_mentioned: Earle H. Warner (Tucson correspondent); Governor of Arizona (letter of safe passage); Theda L. Pobst (poem)
notable_details: In Tucson she appeared on TV made two radio recordings spoke to youth groups at the University of Arizona and to college and high school groups at a large church; stayed in the homes of two teachers a preacher and a Quaker nurse. On her way out of town to mail letters she was picked up by a plain-clothes policeman booked for vagrancy fingerprinted and jailed overnight; next morning she pleaded not guilty and the case was dismissed. Her belongings included a letter from the Governor of Arizona offering safe passage.

Says she recently walked through Lee's Summit MO and stopped at Unity School to speak to the students. Tunic back reads 25000 MILES ON FOOT FOR WORLD PEACE and she has finished walking those miles - so this is 1964 or later. Mentions choosing between nuclear war and a golden age of peace.
date_note: Undated. INDEX DATE WRONG: index says 1950s; content dates it to 1964 or later.

publication: Peace News (London) - same article as row 015
notable_details: Identical to row 015; hand note on clipping: From an English paper !?

route_before: Los Angeles

notable_details: Described as a thirtyish California woman calling herself a Pilgrim for Peace; walked through Cumberland yesterday; interviewed by a local radio station; devoting the entire year to the journey.
date_note: Undated; late 1953 (between Pittsburgh area and Washington DC). State not named; Cumberland MD fits the route.

miles_reported: 1,000 from Los Angeles; two pairs of shoes worn out

Says she gets the best reception from ministers and GIs (soldiers at one army camp came out by the hundreds). An anonymous $10 for clothing waited for her at general delivery in Tucson. Says she worked for years with the American Friends Society in Philadelphia; mailing address Cologne NJ.
date_note: Undated; a Sunday in mid/late March 1953 (between Tucson ~Mar 2 and Abilene Apr 17).

route_before: Stepped out of Los Angeles Jan 1
route_planned: Dallas - Kansas City - St. Louis - Chicago - Detroit; New York City in December
notable_details: Shuffled into El Paso ending a 1000-mile lap. Once someone paid for an expensive hotel suite; the next night she slept on the concrete floor of an all-night gas station; sometimes borrows a blanket from campers and sleeps in the desert. One of her three petitions is circulating in foreign countries.
date_note: Undated; same visit as row 032 (mid/late March 1953). Hand-stamped El Paso Herald-Post.

route_before: Left Los Angeles Jan 1
route_planned: New York; deliver petitions to the President and the UN
notable_details: Walked into Abilene late Thursday afternoon (April 16). Only twice has she had to walk all night. Accepts no rides; money she is given pays for printing more peace messages. Third petition addressed to whomever you believe has the power to end the war in Korea.

miles_reported: 5,000 (planned); three pairs of shoes worn out

miles_reported: 2,100; on her fourth pair of shoes

notable_details: In Wichita Tuesday contacting people whose names she got from peace-minded people further west. At Pasadena she had no money for a costume so walked alongside the parade crowd handing out petitions. Says her appearance at Pasadena touched off an FBI investigation. Arrested twice for vagrancy on the trip (would not name the towns). In hot weather walks at night and sleeps by day. Sunday night slept under a tree near Wellington; breakfast was cherries picked from a tree. Was once a typist; hitchhiked from New Jersey to Pasadena to start the pilgrimage.

miles_reported: almost 2,500; four pairs of shoes worn out

notable_details: Walked into Topeka on Friday (June 26). Wore blue slacks blue blouse and a jacket lettered Peace Pilgrim on the front and walking coast to coast for peace on the back. Has never gone a day without food; spent only two nights walking because she had no place to sleep.

miles_reported: 5,000 (planned); on fourth pair of shoes; 25 mi/day

route_before: Los Angeles

notable_details: Walked through the Chicago Loop. Said her home is Cologne NJ. Dedicated her life to God 15 years ago. Her creed lets her ride in vehicles only within cities; on the open road she refuses all rides.

In cities she uses transport to reach radio and TV dates then returns to the point she left off to continue on foot. A friend made a replacement tunic that waited at General Delivery in Dallas; two more tunics have awaited her since.

Stopped in the News-Journal newsroom.

Five feet four 115 pounds; accent of someone from between Brooklyn and Baltimore; says all three wire services have been very kind. Photo shows her pointing at a map of her route.

notable_details: Walked into pre-Christmas Newark this morning with $1.57 in her pockets. Made the trip TO California by hitchhiking. Jailed twice for vagrancy: in Arizona (warm shower clean bed; released when police found the Governor's letter) and in Texas (a crowded cell where she counselled a runaway teenage girl; released next day after a local clergyman vouched for her). Police often found her shelter in town halls fire houses and police stations. Once in the Midwest woke by the roadside to find a wheat combine bearing down on her. Says she intends to live in voluntary poverty and has no permanent home.

route_before: Just completed the walk from Los Angeles to New York

Says she takes only salaried jobs below the income tax threshold so she does not support war bonds; believes strongly in Jesus Christ and the scriptures. Hand note: After completion of her 1st coast to coast walk.
date_note: Undated; late December 1953 or January 1954 (New York).

route_before: Came through Washington DC on the hike from Los Angeles to New York
notable_details: News note: she came through Washington but failed to get an interview with President Eisenhower.
date_note: Undated; late 1953/early 1954. Hand-labelled The Churchman (Episcopal) N.Y.

route_before: Last few days terribly cold; imprisoned 13 hours in an icy station rest room; sixth shoe came apart and was repaired with airplane tape; after dark walked the narrow catwalk across the Skyway over Newark
route_planned: In New York; hopes to present the disarmament petition to Madam Pandit at the UN
people_mentioned: Madam Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit (UN General Assembly president)
notable_details: Completed the trek December 17 1953 and has been busy with speaking engagements since. All wire services and TV carried the story. Considers this only the beginning of her work.

route_before: Recently finished 5000 miles border to border and coast to coast
route_planned: Speak Feb 27 at 8 pm at Horsham Friends Meeting House
notable_details: Has spoken to many groups in this area.

route_before: Los Angeles to New York City in 1953
people_mentioned: Mrs. Edith Wood (Hatboro); Joseph Geder and Mrs. Elsie Geder (Willow Grove); Phillip Reeves (Warminster); Robert Nelson (Fulmor Heights)
notable_details: Photo: guest speaker at a recent meeting of the Horsham Friends Meeting House in Horsham township.
date_note: Masthead Wednesday afternoon March 3 1954; talk was Feb 27 1954 (see row 071).

miles_reported: 5,000 (planned); at least 100 miles in each state
route_planned: Second pilgrimage starting in California on January 1 1955
notable_details: Announces the 1955 pilgrimage (prayer and penance for world disarmament). Asks volunteers in each state to watch for her and report her itinerary.

publication: Mirror-News Los Angeles (by Phyllis Beardsley religion editor)
route_before: Began two years ago at the Pasadena Rose Parade
route_planned: Visit the capital of every state in the next two years; walks tomorrow in the Rose Parade; Sunday speaks at Pasadena Friends Church
notable_details: Last night (New Year's Eve) attended the Watch Night service at Mt. Hollywood Congregational Church. Paper says she was a secretary 15 years ago and had a Quaker background in New England (contradicted by other sources). New tunic reads Walking 10000 Miles for World Disarmament.
date_note: Masthead Saturday January 1 1955 (photo caption says walks tomorrow in the Rose Parade - the parade was Mon Jan 3 1955 because Jan 1 was a Saturday... see note).

publication: Los Angeles Times (by Dan L. Thrapp religion editor)
miles_reported: 5,000 in 1953; seven pairs of shoes worn out
route_before: First 5000-mile hike from Jan. 1 1953; tried to enter Canada but immigration refused her as not self-supporting
route_planned: This week began a new trek walking at least 100 miles in each state and hitchhiking between them
notable_details: Born on a New Jersey farm 50 or more years ago; relatives in Cologne NJ. Worked for the Friends for 15 years mostly in office work. Describes a night walking in a New Jersey woodland that led to her calling; later a 45-day fast. A policeman at the Pasadena Rose Bowl the other day told her we need people like you.

route_before: Crossed the Golden Gate Bridge Monday (paid a dime at the pedestrian turnstile); night in Ignacio; walking on Tuesday along Sears Point Road
route_planned: San Francisco to Sacramento on a 100-mile pilgrimage; will do the same in every state
notable_details: Walked through the north end of Vallejo Tuesday afternoon (Jan 11). Carries no food or knapsack - only a toothbrush and comb.
date_note: Masthead Wednesday January 12 1955; walk-through Tuesday January 11. Index file name says Jan17.

miles_reported: 1,500 so far on this trek (14 states and Mexico); shoes good for 1300 miles
route_before: Started from Huron on Friday; little drinking water between Blunt and Pierre; arrived in Pierre Monday night
route_planned: Walk 100 miles in every US state and in Canada and Mexico ending at each capital; 3700 miles remaining
people_mentioned: A local woman who planned to buy her new shoes
notable_details: Arrived in Pierre (state capital) Monday night after hiking from Huron. Carries everything in the pockets of a sleeveless jacket. Has traveled up to 50 miles in 24 hours.
date_note: Undated; mid-1955 (after 14 states; before Mitchell SD July 2). Index label says Huron but the article reports from Pierre.

miles_reported: 5,000 in 1953 (200 days); 800 since leaving San Francisco in January; eight pairs of shoes
route_before: Left San Francisco last January; walked to Denver from Pueblo; once slept on the front seat of a fire engine in Tucson
route_planned: Leave for Cheyenne next Monday; 100 miles in each state to its capitol then may ride
notable_details: Arrived in Denver Monday (April 25). Says the Lord gave her the name Peace Pilgrim when she dedicated her life 15 years ago. Says she fasted 45 days in North Carolina taking only water after the third day.

miles_reported: 6,500 since 1953; ninth pair of shoes this year
route_before: Second half: walking 100 miles at a time toward each state capitol and accepting rides between
route_planned: 10000 miles by 1956
notable_details: Stopped in Mitchell Tuesday evening. Photo shows her reading newspaper clippings about herself. Peace messages are printed by friends and forwarded to each capitol. Her goals were peace in Korea and a peace department; since those (she believes) were met her aim is world disarmament.
date_note: Masthead Wednesday July 2[0 or 7] 1955 (day digit cut off; index says July 2 but July 2 1955 was a Saturday). Stop was Tuesday July 19 or 26.

publication: Milwaukee Sentinel (Chapter and Verse by Paul E. Gustafson)
route_before: Arrived in Milwaukee for the first time Thursday after a walk from Racine
route_planned: Hike on to Madison; aims to visit the governor of every state
notable_details: Described as about 48. Tells the story of the rough man in a car in the Arizona desert at night who said he could not touch her after she fell asleep trustingly. Accepts rides between walks. Continued in row 082.
date_note: Masthead Saturday August 20 1955; arrived Thursday August 18.

notable_details: Says she was once investigated by the FBI and spent 24 hours behind bars. Claims her petitions started the push for a peace department in the President's cabinet.

miles_reported: 6,500 on first journey (1953-54); 20 mi/day on the road
route_before: Left Milwaukee early Tuesday; talked with a young man at Goerke's Corners; reached Waukesha city limits about 6 pm Tuesday
route_planned: Madison (her Wisconsin destination) on Thursday
notable_details: Tunic now reads Walking 10000 Miles for World Disarmament. Says she was an office worker for 15 years before devoting her life to service. In 1954 she went through a 45-day period of prayer and fasting; a top-level conference in Canada between Eisenhower and Churchill prompted her to end it. Second coast-to-coast journey began early this year in San Francisco. Spends about 10 days of every two weeks addressing church student and women's groups.
date_note: Masthead Wednesday evening August 24 1955; visit Tuesday August 23.

route_planned: Starting back on the second leg; visit each state capital and walk at least 100 miles in each state
people_mentioned: Rev. G. S. Nichols (host)
notable_details: In Ames this week. Will talk at Collegiate Methodist church Sunday at 8 pm. Talks disarmament world government and religion.

publication: Lincoln Evening Journal and Nebraska State Journal
route_before: Came from Iowa; slept out only two nights in Nebraska
route_planned: Speak 5:30 pm Sunday at the Church of the Brethren then go to Kansas
notable_details: Arrived at the Nebraska Capitol completing 7000 miles. Photo striding by 48th and O streets beside US 34 and Nebraska 2 highway signs. Gray-haired native of New Jersey.

miles_reported: 7,200 in under two years; ~200 miles in each state
route_before: Friday entered Warrensburg; Saturday set out for Sedalia; Sunday left for Syracuse (slept on a pool table); Monday left for California MO; Tuesday 25-mile walk from California MO arriving 6 pm
route_planned: St. Louis (accepting rides) for prearranged speaking dates
people_mentioned: Mr. and Mrs. James Keefe (hosts; Old St. Louis Rd.); Gov. Phil M. Donnelly (hoped to visit)
notable_details: Arrived in Jefferson City about 6 pm yesterday (Tuesday Nov 8): last leg of her 200-mile sojourn through Missouri. Hails from Cologne NJ. Has slept in gas stations fire engines shacks and once a suite.

route_before: Recently spoke at Washington University in St. Louis
route_planned: On her way to Arkansas
people_mentioned: Gary Adamson family (hosts; 1349 Washington)
notable_details: In Springfield this weekend resting at the Adamson home. Declines to use her real name because I'm just an unknown.
date_note: Undated; a weekend in mid-November 1955 (after Jefferson City Nov 8 and St. Louis; before Little Rock Nov 27).

notable_details: Arrived yesterday in Kansas City. Photo shows the tunic back reading Walking 10000 Miles for World Disarmament.
date_note: Dated Nov. 2 1955 per caption; arrived Nov 1.

route_before: Wednesday night: Clarksville sitting in a chair with head on a table; Thursday night: cement floor of the Courthouse at Russellville; Friday: a parked car at Morrilton; Saturday: a home at Conway; Sunday night: North Little Rock
route_planned: Talk with Governor Faubus; speak at schools and Little Rock Junior College before leaving Wednesday
people_mentioned: Dr. and Mrs. Johan Eliot (hosts; 204 East C St. North Little Rock); Governor Orval Faubus
notable_details: Walked into North Little Rock early last night. Talked to sociology and history classes Wednesday (Nov 23) at the University of Arkansas (Fayetteville). Credits the appointment of Harold Stassen as Eisenhower's disarmament assistant as fulfilling her second goal.

route_planned: Through the South for winter: Arkansas Louisiana Mississippi Alabama; north through Tennessee and Kentucky in spring; finish second pilgrimage about Christmas 1956
notable_details: Peace Pilgrim in South: itinerary announcement.
Photo: left Norman today to continue the 10000-mile walk.

miles_reported: 7,400 total; 2,400 this year; 23 states and Mexico; nine pairs of shoes
route_before: Was in Oklahoma City yesterday; walked Tulsa to Oklahoma City on Highway 66 (twice ministers and their wives drove out to find her a bed)
route_planned: Leave Norman about 1 pm today for Louisiana; Christmas Day in Shreveport with a good friend she met in Kansas
people_mentioned: Dr. and Mrs. Henry S. Robinson (hosts; 1027 Berry Road); Dr. R. M. Powell (sociology professor)
notable_details: Spent last night with the Robinsons and talked to Dr. Powell's sociology class this morning at the University of Oklahoma.
date_note: Same day as row 091: Tuesday December 20 1955.

miles_reported: 5,000 in 1953 (200 walking days); 100 miles each in CA AZ NM since January; eighth pair of shoes
route_before: Walked 104 miles from Waco city hall in 3.5 days, sleeping on a gas station floor in a parked car and in a home; arrived Austin Saturday
route_planned: Leave Austin Wednesday toward Mexico; ride to within 100 miles of Mexico City then walk to the capital
people_mentioned: Governor Allan Shivers (hoped to meet)
notable_details: Will speak Tuesday 8 pm at Bethel Temple on The Peace Within. Says she dedicated her life to service 17 years ago. Does not speak Spanish.
date_note: Undated; about March 1955 (after CA AZ NM capitals; before Denver Apr 25).

publication: Oklahoma City Times (photo by Dick Peters)
people_mentioned: Dick Peters (photographer)
notable_details: Photo: tying her ventilated canvas shoes; paused in Oklahoma City.

route_before: Came into Hutchinson with a truck driver and his son
route_planned: Walk 100 miles in Kansas from Abilene to Topeka next weekend; speak Friday night at McPherson
notable_details: Visited briefly Tuesday (Oct 18). Says in 1954 she walked so little she does not count it. No change of clothes - washes what she wears.

route_before: Accepted rides from Tacoma WA to Missoula
route_planned: Leave Monday to walk to Helena arriving Thursday; then see Dr. Harvey F. Baty in Bozeman
people_mentioned: Dr. Deane Ferm (director School of Religion Montana State University; host 510 McLeod Ave.); Dr. Harvey F. Baty of Bozeman (met at a religious conference she addressed in New Hampshire)
notable_details: Arrived Thursday; Friday morning spoke at the University; Friday night to Missoula Friends and local ministers at Dr. Ferm's home; public meeting Sunday 8 pm. Pledged to visit every state capital plus Canada and Mexico.
date_note: Undated; mileage (6200) places it in June 1955 between Denver/Cheyenne and the Dakotas. Index lists it at the end of 1955.

route_planned: Arrive in Vicksburg tonight; reach Jackson by Wednesday; visit Hattiesburg and Gulfport before leaving Mississippi
notable_details: Arrived in Natchez Friday night (Jan 6) and was photographed eating an apple at the Community grocery. Left Natchez Saturday morning. Spends about two weeks in each state.

miles_reported: nine pairs of shoes worn out; about 300 miles on the tenth
route_before: Arrived in Jackson after dark Tuesday by foot from Vicksburg
route_planned: After several days in Jackson travel toward the Gulf Coast then into Alabama
notable_details: Visitor in the capital on Wednesday; Jackson her 25th state capital. INDEX ERROR: listed as Johnson MS - the hand label reads The Clarion Ledger Jackson Mississippi.

publication: State Times (Jackson MS; by George Harmon)
route_before: Mississippi walk began in Natchez; four days to Jackson via Vicksburg: nights in homes at Port Gibson and near Edwards and at Jackson; hotel lobbies at Natchez and Vicksburg; ate pecans along Highways 61 and 80
route_planned: Stay in Jackson over the weekend
people_mentioned: A Jackson woman who stopped her car on the outskirts and hosted her Tuesday night
notable_details: Walked into Jackson last night (Tuesday Jan 10). Says she read of the Korean truce on a teletype while sitting in an Illinois newspaper office (July 1953).
date_note: From front page of State Times Jackson Miss. Wed. Jan. 11 1956.

miles_reported: 7,700; up to 50 miles in a day
route_planned: Leave tomorrow for Birmingham then Tuscaloosa then Tennessee
people_mentioned: C. H. Lancaster Jr. (architect; host 115 S. McDonough St.)
notable_details: Walked into Montgomery last night. Says she dedicated her life 18 years ago.
date_note: Masthead Wednesday January 25 1956; arrived Tuesday Jan 24.

publication: The Nashville Tennessean (photo by Joe Rudis)
route_before: Has zig-zagged the country and dipped into Mexico and Canada; walked into Nashville Friday night
route_planned: Headed up the eastern seaboard
notable_details: Visited the governor's office at the state capitol Saturday (did not see the governor). Photographed in front of artillery shells (weapons of war and a voice of peace). Says she was intrigued by money in school; saw its folly 15 years ago.
date_note: Masthead Sunday morning February 12 1956; arrived Friday Feb 10.

miles_reported: 7,900 since tabulating two years ago; 10,000+ in total
route_before: Tennessee: walked Huntingdon to Nashville and also visited Memphis Jackson Chattanooga and Knoxville; Kentucky: walked Louisville to Frankfort by way of Lexington; recently slept in an all-night restaurant a bus station and a service station floor
route_planned: Indiana next; another year touching Canada and ending in Florida
notable_details: Arrived in Owensboro late yesterday afternoon (Thursday March 1). Will appear on WOMI and WVJS radio and speak at Kentucky Wesleyan College Student Union at 10 am today. Calls the Stassen appointment a vague granting of her second goal.

route_before: Entered Ohio at Cincinnati and walked to Columbus via Dayton and Springfield (her 100 Ohio miles)
route_planned: Accept rides to Clarksburg WV (next state)
notable_details: Came to Columbus today: her 32nd capital and 31st state (the extra capital is Mexico City). Says if mankind has not found peace by 10000 miles she will start a new 5000-mile walk.

miles_reported: 8,000+; 11th pair of shoes; Indiana is 29th state
route_before: Indiana walk began last week at Terre Haute; hiked to Bloomington; two days there; set out for Indianapolis Friday
route_planned: Ride tomorrow to Richmond; then rides to Fort Wayne Goshen and South Bend; Sunday launch her march in Michigan
notable_details: Strolled into Indianapolis yesterday for a two-day visit. Says she marched from San Francisco to New York three years ago (other sources say Los Angeles).
date_note: Undated; about March 1956 (29th state - after Kentucky; before Michigan and Ohio).

route_planned: Walk to New York soon then to Canada; if refused entry walk along the border
people_mentioned: Miss Bertha Faust (host; 709 N. 8th St. Philadelphia)
notable_details: Came striding into The News city room last night (Wednesday May 9).

miles_reported: 8,600; 11 pairs of shoes; 248 miles from Toronto
route_before: Entered Canada at Niagara Falls; visited Toronto; rode to Kingston; walked Kingston to Ottawa (100 miles)
route_planned: Tour the Peace Tower today; leave Tuesday for Montreal; re-enter the US through Vermont
notable_details: Arrived in Ottawa on foot Saturday (June 9). Photographed in front of the Peace Tower at Parliament. Has not skipped a meal in Canada. Sends a newsletter about every six months to about 10000 people.

route_before: Entered Maine at the beginning of July; walked Portland - Freeport - Lewiston - Brunswick - Bath - Wiscasset - Gardiner - Augusta
route_planned: Spend today (Tuesday) in Augusta
notable_details: Arrived in Augusta Monday afternoon (July 9) walking through the rain; a day ahead of schedule. Only one night in Maine sleeping in the open; insoles cut from an old inner tube.
date_note: Hand-dated Daily Kennebec Journal Augusta Maine Tuesday morning July 10 1956.

notable_details: Talked on Boston Common yesterday surrounded by men in hats.
date_note: Dated July 30 1956 per caption; on the Common Sunday July 29.

publication: The North Adams Transcript (by John Douglas)
miles_reported: 3,900 on the second phase; 37 states plus Mexico and Canada; 12 pairs of shoes
route_before: Walked from Great Barrington to Williamstown yesterday (given supper in Adams); night with Rev. and Mrs. Newell Davis of Williamstown First Methodist; Rev. Davis drove her to the base of Mount Greylock
route_planned: After Greylock: Springfield - Worcester - Boston (see Gov. Christian A. Herter); then 100 miles each in Connecticut Rhode Island the middle Atlantic and south coastal states ending in Florida
people_mentioned: Rev. and Mrs. Newell Davis (Williamstown)
notable_details: Hiked up Mount Greylock (Massachusetts' highest peak) as a prayer for world disarmament while the UN Disarmament Commission met in New York. Says she first felt the call to the pilgrimage in 1953 while staying in New England. Reporter claims she had been a psychiatric therapist (not found in other sources).
date_note: Undated; Greylock hike in mid-July 1956 (before Boston July 29).

publication: The Bridgeport Post (by Judith Priestley; photo Mathewson)
miles_reported: 9,100; all but nine states; 12 pairs of shoes; fifth tunic
route_planned: Leave tomorrow morning for New Haven; then Waterbury and Hartford
people_mentioned: Mr. and Mrs. Donald A. Gaines (hosts; 42 Bancroft Ave.)
notable_details: In Bridgeport today; spent last night (Tuesday Aug 14) with the Gaineses whom she contacted through a mutual friend. Tunic pockets hold a sweater scarf road maps and printed messages.

miles_reported: 9,200 (800 left at Hartford); 41 states so far
route_before: Mid-winter blizzard night in the Appalachians spent in a cardboard carton under a bridge
route_planned: Hartford in a day or two; then NJ DE MD VA NC SC GA FL
people_mentioned: A husky walking-club member who walked 33 miles with her
notable_details: Got to Waterbury last night (Tuesday Aug 21). Most luxurious shelter a $15-a-day suite; most luxurious meal at the Waldorf Astoria bought by one of two millionaires she knows. Mail: Peace Pilgrim Cologne N.J.

route_before: Friday night with Dr. and Mrs. Thomas Harvey of Princeton (met her at Hartford last month); last night in Mount Holly with friends
route_planned: Moorestown tomorrow; Trenton Tuesday
people_mentioned: Dr. and Mrs. Thomas Harvey (Princeton)
notable_details: Walked the road to Mount Holly yesterday (Saturday Sept 8). Photo on the grass divider of Route 206 just south of Route 130 beside a Straight for New York 63 sign. Says in 1954 she counted no miles.

miles_reported: 9,675 highway miles (not counting city miles); 12th pair of shoes
route_before: Walked from Greensboro; last night slept in a parked car on the outskirts of Durham (a garage man's offer; a truck driver bought dinner)
route_planned: Tomorrow walk to Raleigh; Thursday Chapel Hill (journalism students at UNC); then South Carolina
notable_details: In Durham today. Has walked through all states except South Carolina Georgia and Florida. Most luxurious lodging a resort hotel in the Southwest; best meal the Waldorf Astoria.

route_planned: Tomorrow walk from Durham to Raleigh; then SC GA FL
notable_details: Photographed walking along a Durham street today.

route_planned: Athens next
people_mentioned: Patrolman J. M. Goodwin
notable_details: Arrived yesterday (Monday Dec 3) on the final leg of her trip. Photo at night asking directions at Broad and Seventh Sts. under US 25 and Georgia 28 signs.

publication: St. Petersburg Times (by Marianne Kelsey; photos Bob Rogers)
route_before: Has visited every state plus Mexico and Canada
route_planned: A lot of walking in Florida; stay a few days in St. Petersburg with friends; on the road again Christmas Day
notable_details: Says she has completed the 10000 miles but does not intend to stop walking. Calls the pilgrimage a calling like some people are called to be ministers.
date_note: Hand-dated St. Petersburg Times Sunday Dec. 23 1956.

miles_reported: 11,000; 100 miles in each Canadian province and in Mexico; 56 months since 1953
route_before: First tried to enter Canada across the Ambassador Bridge and was turned back for lack of funds and no Canadian sponsor; this time carried $100 across and mailed it back from the first post office
route_planned: Address a public meeting Friday 8 pm at Trinity United Church
people_mentioned: Mayor Michael J. Patrick
notable_details: Walked to the mayor's office Thursday morning and suggested the riverfront park be named Peace Park; the mayor promised to put it before City Council. New tunic: 10000 Miles on Foot for World Peace. INDEX DATE WRONG: index says 1957 Jan 26 but the clipping is hand-dated September 26 1957 and says 56 months since Jan 1953 (= Sept 1957).

route_planned: Walk 100 miles in each Canadian province
notable_details: Photo: now visiting Vancouver.

miles_reported: 10,175 (counted); 12 pairs of shoes; six uniforms; 1000 miles planned in Canada
route_before: Walked into Victoria (BC capital) then left; Tuesday night partly walking and partly in an abandoned car between Lethbridge and Fort Macleod; Wednesday night sheltered four hours in the Medicine Hat jail; Wednesday ate four small oranges and Thursday two glasses of milk
route_planned: Spend the weekend in Calgary then leave for Edmonton where mail awaits
notable_details: Walked into Calgary early Friday morning (June 7). Mail awaits her in the capitals of nine provinces. Says in Mexico the language barrier convinced her that her mission was among English-speaking peoples.
date_note: Masthead Friday June 7 1957. Note: the Medicine Hat / Lethbridge nights do not follow a single straight route - the jail stop may be from a different night order.

miles_reported: 10,000 counted; estimates nearly twice that walked
people_mentioned: Fellowship of Reconciliation and Religious Society of Friends (organisers)
notable_details: Monday night (election night June 10 1957) drew about 50 people to a meeting at the public library. Ended with her little magic formula: be concerned that you do not offend not that you are not offended.

miles_reported: 10,000+; 13 pairs of shoes; current pair good for 1500 miles
route_before: Began with Ontario in June 1956 to walk 100 miles in each province; last night stayed with Mr. and Mrs. R. L. Abram (1090 Second Ave. N.E.)
route_planned: Today toward Regina where she expects to speak this week; complete 100 miles in Saskatchewan in the next few days
people_mentioned: Mr. and Mrs. R. L. Abram (hosts)
notable_details: Rested in Moose Jaw's Crescent Park on Sunday afternoon (June 23). Says she was born in the US and eats no fish meat or fowl.

route_before: Will have walked 100 miles in PEI by this morning: Richmond - Charlottetown - Souris; already walked 100 miles in the western provinces
route_planned: 100 miles in each of the other Atlantic provinces plus Quebec and Ontario; talk Wednesday evening at Heartz Memorial Hall
notable_details: Photo walking a rural PEI road.

route_before: Flew to Stephenville Crossing a few days ago; hitch-hiked across Newfoundland; walked 100 miles from LaManche to St. John's
route_planned: Steamer to Nova Scotia on Saturday; still to walk 100 miles in Nova Scotia New Brunswick and Quebec
notable_details: Arrived yesterday morning. Meeting Friday 8 pm at Gower Street United Church Lecture Hall. Forwarding address Cologne NJ. Wears blue shirt windbreaker and jeans. Appears about 45.
date_note: Undated; between PEI (July 22) and Quebec (Sept 1) - about early August 1957. Confirms St. John's Newfoundland.

route_before: Walking the Topsail Road yesterday morning to end a 100-mile walk
notable_details: Says she has abandoned her family name and family: all peoples of the world are her brothers and sisters.
date_note: Undated; same day as row 121 (about early August 1957).

notable_details: French-language front-page headline only (Incredible pilgrimage of a mysterious woman). Article text not in scan.

route_before: Florida walk began in Pensacola: Panama City - Tallahassee - other cities - High Springs - Gainesville; has walked every state every Canadian province and into Mexico
notable_details: Passed through Gainesville yesterday; checked her 39 pieces of mail on the post office steps. Says she was born in the United States. Index lists this under 1957; mileage (11350 vs 10175 in June 1957 and 13500 in Jan 1959) and all provinces done place it in late 1957 or 1958.

miles_reported: 17th pair of shoes; about 2000 mi/year (1000 summer in the northern US; 1000 winter in the west)
route_before: Spoke last week (Friday night) at the Town House on Pacific Avenue to Understanding Unit No. 9
route_planned: Walking to Palo Alto then San Francisco then Sacramento then back to Los Angeles
notable_details: Visited The Sentinel that afternoon. New tunic: Walking 25000 Miles for World Peace. Has not had a headache or cold in six years. Writer guesses she was once a dancer.
date_note: Masthead Thursday December 18 1958; talk Friday December 12.

miles_reported: 13,500 since January 1953; 16 pairs of shoes; 48 states 10 provinces and Mexico
route_before: Yesterday walked 20 miles from the San Francisco main post office along Highway 101 to San Rafael
route_planned: Today in rain and wind left for Vallejo
people_mentioned: Rev. and Mrs. Ervin C. Tipton (hosts; 25 Sunset Way San Rafael)
notable_details: Says When God gives you a name you don't ask for any other. Says I am ageless. Her first petition was for an end to fighting in Korea.
date_note: Hand-dated San Rafael CA Independent Journal 01-05-59; arrived Sunday January 4 1959.

miles_reported: 13,550 counted; 17th pair of shoes; 5000 the first year now about 2000/year
route_before: 100-mile route from San Francisco via the Golden Gate Bridge and Marin County (no foot traffic on the Bay Bridge); walked into Sacramento from Davis yesterday about 5 pm
route_planned: Stay until Wednesday then travel to Stockton
people_mentioned: Friends she met on her 1955 visit (hosts)
notable_details: Arrived Sunday (Jan 11) almost four years to the day after her 1955 visit. Speaking engagement Wednesday 8 pm at the chapel of Pioneer Congregational Church 2700 L Street. Says she was born in this country; 5 ft 4 in; 115 lb; hair already silver in 1953.

miles_reported: 14,000 (paper says since New Year's Day 1952 - an error for 1953)
route_planned: In San Diego two weeks
notable_details: Hiked into San Diego yesterday (Monday March 16). Recommends a world language as the biggest single step toward peace.

route_planned: Stay in the Orange area through Sunday; may speak to a church group
people_mentioned: Mrs. Laura Warren and Nora Turner (hostesses; Orange residents)
notable_details: Visiting the Orange area this week; Thursday spoke to the Chapman College student body. Says friends who heard her speak elsewhere invited her.
date_note: Hand-dated The Orange Daily News Friday April 10 1959.

miles_reported: 14,225 (walked miles only); 175 in Washington so far
route_before: Arrived in Washington state May 25
people_mentioned: A Zillah family (hosts last night)
notable_details: Arrived in Yakima yesterday (Tuesday June 23). Says she took a vow of simplicity 15 years before she started walking. Never skipped more than four meals in a row; about three-fourths of the time she sleeps in a bed.

publication: Capital Journal (Salem OR; by Alfred C. Jones)
route_before: First of five visits to Salem was May 15 1959 (photo with the old City Hall clock tower)
route_planned: In Salem four more days; return June 28 at 8 pm to speak at Unity of Salem (1361 Madison St. NE) on The Steps Toward Inner Peace
people_mentioned: Concerned Citizens for Peace (Sunday meeting sponsor)
notable_details: INDEX DATE WRONG: this is a later article (writer recalls his 1959 interview from 14 years ago; she says 35 years since she started living to give; lettering now factory-made). The same file is the 1973 June 18 Salem entry (row 199). Reports a 1959 Salem visit on May 15.

route_planned: Free public meeting Tuesday 8 pm at Pasco First Congregational Church (Henry and Aurelia Sts.)
people_mentioned: Rev. and Mrs. Paul Sutley (Congregational Church; invited her)
notable_details: Walked into Pasco Sunday (June 28). Waves to motorists facing traffic. Mail: Peace Pilgrim Cologne NJ.

publication: The Billings Gazette (by Addison R. Bragg)
route_before: Montana part ended earlier this week in Helena after walking from Spokane
route_planned: Next walk from Idaho Falls to Salt Lake City starting after she leaves Billings Friday; public meeting Thursday 8 pm at First Baptist Church
people_mentioned: Friends she made on a visit four years ago
notable_details: Arrived in Billings late Tuesday (Aug 4) for two days. Checked 100+ letters at the Billings post office (from Canada California Florida Ohio Oregon and a dozen more states; one from an embassy in Washington). Reporter says her accent is New England or at least eastern.

miles_reported: 14,550; 1000 miles through the northwest this summer
route_planned: Leave Thursday for Boise; then begin a walk to Salt Lake City
people_mentioned: Mrs. Murl Gidel (host; 1127 W. Mercury)
notable_details: Visiting Butte; public meeting Thursday 2 pm in the YMCA Fellowship Room. Diet: fruits nuts vegetables whole grain milk and cheese. Mail forwarded by a woman in Cologne NJ; a woman in Pennsylvania puts out her semi-annual newsletter.

route_planned: Leave Thursday for Boise; begin a walk to Salt Lake City
people_mentioned: Mrs. Murl Gidel (host; 1127 W. Mercury)
notable_details: Same text as row 134 (Butte Daily Post). YMCA talk Thursday 2 pm.

publication: The Herald Journal (Logan UT; by Edith Morgan)
route_before: Monday evening sheltered from rain on a porch between Smithfield and Richmond and was invited in by Mrs. Dexter Kent (meal and lodging); one night spoke at the 15th Ward Mutual and stayed with Mrs. Josephine Christensen; walked to Brigham City; next day to Roy where she spoke; then to Ogden; Saturday spoke in Bountiful
route_planned: Today (Sunday) in Salt Lake City
people_mentioned: Mrs. Dexter Kent; Mrs. Josephine Christensen; Edith Morgan (reporter)
notable_details: Photographed walking between Smithfield and Logan this week near a Logan Cache Airport sign. Says the postmistress in Cologne NJ offered to be a clearing house for her mail.

route_before: Wound up a 1000-mile pilgrimage of the northwestern states and Nevada
route_planned: Soon start another 1000-mile trek of Arizona and New Mexico
notable_details: Walked into Las Vegas yesterday. Photo pointing on a map to how she came into Las Vegas. Took her vow of simplicity 15 years before the pilgrimage began.
date_note: Undated; between Salt Lake City (Sept 20) and Prescott (Oct 28) 1959.

notable_details: Photo with the map; same visit as row 137.

miles_reported: 15,000+; 5000 in 1953; uncounted 1954; another 5000 in 1955-56; now about 2000 per year (1000 north in summer and 1000 south in winter)
route_before: Came yesterday by way of Jerome; first stop in Prescott though she has been in Arizona three times
route_planned: Stay one week with Mr. and Mrs. Fred Ryan at the Tall Trees Motel; then walk down US 89 to Phoenix; walk in Arizona and New Mexico this winter
people_mentioned: Mr. and Mrs. Fred Ryan (Tall Trees Motel)
notable_details: Walked into Prescott Wednesday (Oct 28). Says she would stop counting at 25000 but continue the pilgrimage. Says most ministers and college professors understand her pilgrimage.

Profile. Says in her youth she had no religious training and grew up outside the church; in student days thought the way to live was to make money; tells of walking all night until at dawn in a clearing she prayed Use me; since that day twenty years ago she has not had a cold or headache.
date_note: Hand-dated Nov. 1959 (Fellowship magazine of the Fellowship of Reconciliation).

notable_details: Sets out her twelve steps to inner peace (four preparations four purifications four relinquishments). Says she has been jailed twice: once overnight for protective custody and once for 24 hours.

people_mentioned: William B. Prothero (poem Candle)
notable_details: Tells of a snowstorm night on a lonely road when she found a large packing box of dry paper under a bridge and slept in it; and the desert night with the rough man in a parked car. Calls peace an idea whose time has come.

publication: Evening Outlook - Bay Area News (Santa Monica)
route_planned: Heading for Arizona and more walking
notable_details: Walked into Santa Monica this week and is speaking here. Since the first year walks 1000 miles in the north in summer and 1000 in the south in winter. Credits Khrushchev's US trip and Eisenhower's tours abroad with bringing peace closer.

route_before: Walked 18 miles from Bernalillo in half a day (Friday)
route_planned: Remain a week; talks Sunday 8 pm (Central Methodist Young Adults) and Thursday 7:30 pm at Geneva House (1820 Las Lomas NE)
people_mentioned: Misses Marion and Catherine Crissey (hosts; 909 Seventh NW)
notable_details: Arrived Friday (March 25). Three-point programme: a world language; a US peace department; commend the good wherever you find it.

route_before: Walked from Albuquerque (left Friday) and arrived in Grants Sunday
route_planned: Public meeting tonight 8 pm at the Methodist Church (The attainment of inner peace and world peace)
notable_details: Says she has enjoyed perfect health for the past 22 years; follows a summer-north winter-south itinerary. Confirms Grants New Mexico (index says PA).
date_note: Index date April 18 1960 (Monday); arrived Sunday April 17.

publication: The Daily Republic (Mitchell SD; by Art Raymond)
route_before: Second appearance in Mitchell (first about five years ago)
route_planned: Going east generally; hopes to end her 25000 miles at Washington DC; tonight public meeting at First Methodist Church
notable_details: Visiting Mitchell Thursday and Friday. Says it is better to light one candle than to curse the darkness. Says she had been in service work for about 15 years before the pilgrimage and did not know the day before that she would begin it.

publication: The Daily Republic (Mitchell SD; photo by Raymond)
notable_details: Photo of row 146: seated in Mitchell.

route_planned: Speak 7:30 pm Wednesday at First Baptist Church (421 Park Ave.)
notable_details: Explained her walk here Monday (Aug 29). Says one night in the Colorado mountains she nearly froze to death but huddled under old newspapers until morning. Says all churches (Christian Buddhist Moslem) are stepping stones to God.
Caption of row 148.

route_planned: Talk Wednesday 7:30 pm at First Baptist Church
notable_details: Text column of row 148.

route_before: Arrived in Tyler Friday (Dec 2)
route_planned: Trek to Dallas next
notable_details: Says she carries her toothbrush in her slacks pocket; her sunsuit serves as nightgown and swimsuit.

route_before: Arrived in Tyler Friday
route_planned: Trek to Dallas
notable_details: INDEX ERROR: listed as 1960 Dec 12 Fort Worth but the link opens a second copy of the Tyler Dec 3 article with photo (holding a map of Texas).

miles_reported: 17,900 in eight years; 1000-mile Texas walk this winter
route_before: Texas: Fort Worth - Dallas - San Antonio - Brownsville - Corpus Christi - Beaumont - back to Houston; strolled into Houston from Baytown Tuesday (Mar 7)
route_planned: Here a week (talks at the Wheeler St. YMCA and churches); then off to the West
people_mentioned: Mr. and Mrs. Walter Whitsun (hosts; 2336 N. Boulevard)
notable_details: Seen chatting with bystanders on a downtown corner this week. Says she first realized inner peace 23 years ago; vegetarian for 18 years.

miles_reported: 18,000 in eight years; 23rd pair of shoes (about 1500 miles each)
route_before: Completed a 1000-mile walking tour of Texas
people_mentioned: A friendly Ysleta couple (overnight hosts); a gas station operator who remembered her from her first tour
notable_details: Stopped overnight in Ysleta. Says before she started walking she had never walked more than five miles.

miles_reported: 18,000+; second trip through Iowa; spending the whole month of May in Iowa
route_before: Thursday night picked up near the Van Horne corner south of Vinton on US 218 by a Cedar Rapids church; spoke there and slept in Cedar Rapids; driven back early this morning to resume
route_planned: Tonight near the junction of US 218 and Iowa 8 for another talk; weekend in Traer with a church group; then walk to Waterloo for mail
notable_details: Passed through Vinton today. Last time she slept in the open was last June. Plans to end her walk in Washington DC.

publication: Cedar Valley Daily Times (end of article)
notable_details: Final lines of row 155.

miles_reported: 18,000+ by Sioux City next week; 200 miles in each of five midwest states this summer
route_before: Wednesday left Waterloo; hitch-hiked to Charles City; broadcast there; continued to Mason City
route_planned: Leave Iowa next week at Sioux City; walk from St. Cloud to Duluth MN
people_mentioned: Ray Smith (librarian Mason City Public Library)
notable_details: Spent Wednesday afternoon (May 24) in Mason City; wrote letters at the public library. Reporter guesses her age as middle or late 60s.

publication: The Sioux City Journal (photo by Paltz)
route_before: Arrived during the weekend from Fort Dodge after crossing Iowa in May
route_planned: Public gathering 7:30 pm tonight at First Methodist Church (Peace Within and Without); stay through Memorial Day
people_mentioned: Miss Ethel Chesterman (hostess Sunday night); Robert J. Zoernig and Harland Soper households
notable_details: Second visit to Sioux City. Adds a third step: an unarmed peace corps.

publication: St. Paul Pioneer Press (by William J. Martin)
miles_reported: 18,000 counted; 22 pairs of shoes (children's size six)
route_before: Last visit to St. Paul about five years ago
route_planned: A week in the Twin Cities then walk to St. Cloud and Duluth
notable_details: Paused in St. Paul Thursday (June 8). Says 49 states (not 48) plus 10 provinces and parts of Mexico; some community peace groups have formed in her wake. Only twice in eight years picked up by police for questioning. Has not slept by the roadside in a year.
date_note: Hand-dated St. Paul Pioneer Press Fri. June 9 1961.

route_before: Spending most of June in Minnesota; has covered the southern part of the state; arrived in St. Cloud Sunday night (lodged at Hotel St. Cloud)
route_planned: Expects to finish 25000 miles in 1964 and end in Washington DC
notable_details: Spent today in St. Cloud. Delighted with the new Peace Corps. Since entering Minnesota has always had a bed and three meals a day.

miles_reported: about 18,000 in eight years; 23 pairs of shoes
route_before: Came to Winona Wednesday a stranger
route_planned: Left this morning for the Twin Cities; then walk to St. Cloud and Duluth
notable_details: Spoke at a joint meeting of Winona's four service clubs (Kiwanis Rotary Lions Exchange) as an unscheduled substitute for Gov. Elmer L. Andersen who could not come because of weather; also on the radio. A man slipped 50 cents into her pocket. A police detective questioned her and the police asked if she was connected with the American Legion convention carnival; one critic said she was an agent of the Kremlin.
date_note: Undated; early June 1961 (before St. Paul June 8). Vegetarian; wears no leather shoes.

route_before: Entered Wisconsin at La Crosse earlier this month; walked to Eau Claire - Wausau - Green Bay - Appleton - Oshkosh - Fond du Lac - Manitowoc; left Manitowoc Saturday and walked into Sheboygan Sunday evening; spent August walking in Minnesota
route_planned: Today or tonight toward Port Washington; then Milwaukee - Racine - Kenosha - Beloit - Janesville - Madison; Illinois in October; Missouri in November
people_mentioned: Chuck Fisher (reporter; host Sunday night); Mrs. Herman Gutenberger (4209 Lake Shore Rd.; dinner)
notable_details: Walked into Sheboygan Sunday evening (Sept 10). Spends three months of each year on a lecture tour.

route_before: Came from Green Bay with stops at Oshkosh and Fond du Lac
route_planned: Sheboygan; Milwaukee next week; Racine and Kenosha; Madison; Illinois; Missouri in November; Louisiana in February. Does not walk in July/August and December (speaking tours)
notable_details: Walked into Manitowoc Friday morning (Sept 8). Mails any money given her to a close friend in Pennsylvania who publishes her free newsletter.
date_note: Undated; Friday September 8 1961 (day before she left for Sheboygan).

publication: Wisconsin State Journal (Madison; by A. Lee Beier)
miles_reported: 18,600 in eight years; 24 pairs of shoes
route_before: Walked Saturday from a point between Edgerton and Stoughton to Madison; has visited every Wisconsin city over 25000 population in the past month
route_planned: Remain through Tuesday; then Illinois
people_mentioned: Mrs. Ernest R. Anderson (1822 Chadbourne Ave.) and Signe Anderson (1907 Birge Terrace) (hostesses)
notable_details: Arrived Saturday afternoon (Sept 23). Addressed a public meeting at Bashford Methodist Church Sunday. Previously visited Madison in 1955 and 1957. Has been in all states but Alaska.

route_before: Last night spoke at First Methodist Church in Bushnell then brought to Peoria by car; came through Wisconsin
route_planned: Tomorrow walk to Pekin then Bloomington; then Missouri
people_mentioned: Dr. and Mrs. Robert Chapman (1000 W. Moss Ave.; Society of Friends meeting host)
notable_details: Came to Peoria this morning (Oct 19). Public gathering at 8 tonight at the Chapman home. Last visit to Peoria was September 1955. Says she is a native of New Jersey.

miles_reported: 24 pairs of shoes in nine-plus years; up to 50 mi/day
route_before: Spent several days in Fort Wayne speaking; part of Saturday in Huntington then walked on to Roanoke
route_planned: Returned Sunday morning to Roanoke to continue from where she stopped
people_mentioned: Mr. and Mrs. O. P. Land (hosts; R.R. 2 Huntington; Mrs. Land met her at Camp Mack in 1956)
notable_details: Walked into Roanoke shortly after 5 pm Saturday (April 21). INDEX ERROR: listed as Roanoke VA; the masthead reads Roanoke Indiana. Has not slept by the roadside in over a year nor walked all night in a year and a half.
date_note: Masthead Thursday April 26 1962; visit Saturday April 21 1962.

route_before: Has crossed Arkansas twice; first time through Stamps and Lafayette County
notable_details: Walked through Stamps early Monday afternoon. Reporter guesses early fifties. Says her faith came about 25 years ago and the vow to walk 10 years later.
date_note: Hand-dated Lewisville Herald with a partly illegible date in 1962 (possibly April 8). Spelling on clipping 25 0000 miles.

miles_reported: 20,000+; 25th pair of shoes; three times across the continent
route_planned: Speak 7:45 pm tomorrow (Sunday) at Broadway Methodist Church chapel and 10 am at Old Bethel Methodist Church
notable_details: Takes rides only to speaking places; on this trip stops at cities over 25000.

publication: Sea Coast Echo (Bay St. Louis MISSISSIPPI)
people_mentioned: Manuel Maurigi (shoe repair specialist; inspected her shoes); August Scafidi (gave food); Bea Georgi (motel room)
notable_details: Passed through Bay St. Louis Saturday afternoon (Feb 9). INDEX ERROR: listed as St. Louis MO; the clipping is from Bay St. Louis Mississippi.
date_note: Hand-dated Sea Coast Echo Bay St. Louis Miss. Feb. 14 1963.

miles_reported: three-quarters of 25,000; every state except Alaska and Hawaii
route_before: Easter Sunday noon in Corfu (lunch with Mr. and Mrs. George M. Arnold and Mrs. Alice Jenner); speaking engagements in Buffalo last week; overnight with Mr. and Mrs. William Gratwick of Linwood
route_planned: Third cross-country walk visiting every sizeable city
people_mentioned: Mrs. Vera Adams (256 Bank St.; photo); Mr. and Mrs. William Gratwick (Linwood)
notable_details: Arrived in Batavia Sunday and found The News office closed; returned Monday morning.

route_planned: Log her 25000th mile walking into Washington DC in October
people_mentioned: Henry Martin (Ocean County Sun reporter)
notable_details: Photo: the reporter walks with her during her recent visit to Toms River and Ocean County.
date_note: Undated; summer 1964 (June-July; before the October finish).

publication: The Charlotte Observer (p.4-A; photo by Hank Daniel)
notable_details: Photo only: walking a Charlotte sidewalk.

publication: The Times-Herald (Newport News VA; by Madeline Duval)
miles_reported: almost 25,000; 12th tunic; 29th pair of shoes; 48 states visited
route_before: Second time in Virginia; first time in the Peninsula area. Yesterday spoke at Grace Methodist Church and to prayer groups
route_planned: Tonight 7:30 First Presbyterian Church Hampton; tomorrow 10:30 am First Methodist Church Newport News; Washington in October to complete 25000 miles
people_mentioned: Mayor Donald Hyatt (photo)
notable_details: Spending three days on the Peninsula (third walking tour visiting every city over 25000). Signs of approaching peace: the test-ban treaty and the Peace Corps.
Photo of row 175: arrived here yesterday.

publication: New Brunswick Daily Home News (by John Murphy)
route_before: Left Plainfield about 9 am; walked via Dunellen - New Market - Edison - Highland Park; arrived about 1 pm yesterday (Tuesday June 16); met newsmen at the Roger Smith Hotel
route_planned: Perth Amboy tomorrow; Long Branch this weekend; July-August speaking in New England; September-October Maryland and Delaware; arrive in Washington DC October 28 to end the 25000-mile pilgrimage
notable_details: Says she broke her 45-day fast in 1954 when Eisenhower and Churchill held preliminary disarmament talks. Calls Sen. Barry Goldwater a dangerous man to be president.
date_note: Hand-dated New Brunswick Daily Home News Weds. 17 June 64.

people_mentioned: Sgt. Edward Sutter (White House Police)
notable_details: Photo: chatting with a White House policeman at the gate; hoped to see President Johnson (away campaigning).
date_note: Masthead Sunday November 1 1964 (photo taken in Washington DC about Oct 28-31).

publication: The Miami Herald (by Jerry Parker; photos Maurice Holley Jr.)
route_before: First pilgrimage zig-zag Los Angeles to New York; second included 48 states Canada and Mexico; third stopped at every city over 25000 in the US and Canada and ended walking into Washington DC last Oct. 28
route_planned: Speaking tour and catching up on correspondence
notable_details: Datelined Palm Beach. Friday spoke at the Royal Poinciana Chapel in Palm Beach; Wednesday and Thursday at Unity of the Palm Beaches and Palm Beach Junior College. Describes the inspiration: a time alone with God high on a hill when she saw herself in the garb of her mission and a map of the US with a jagged line across it. Confirms she ended the 25000 miles walking into Washington DC on Oct 28 1964.

route_before: First pilgrimage launched at the Tournament of Roses parade 13 years ago: she stepped in front of the marchers and walked ahead of the parade its entire route; third pilgrimage walked into and out of every US city over 25000
route_planned: Speaking engagements around Los Angeles by car; first is Sunday 2:30 pm at the Pasadena Science of Mind Church
notable_details: Back in Los Angeles; explained Thursday (Dec 30). Has been picked up for vagrancy a number of times. One person she talked to in Washington turned out to be a presidential aide. Says you can hardly walk on freeways anymore.

publication: Santa Fe New Mexican (story and pictures by Richard Polese)
notable_details: Last week visited Santa Fe and spoke at La Posada the College of Santa Fe and St. John's College (photo with students at a dining-hall table). Says the real cause of war is immaturity.
date_note: Credit line: Santa Fe N. Mex. News October 13 1966; visit the week before (about Oct 3-9 1966).

publication: Chicago Tribune (Front Views and Profiles by Kay Loring; Tribune staff photo)
route_before: Within the last few weeks walked Kansas City to St. Louis then to Champaign and on to Chicago
route_planned: In Chicago until about May 22; downtown talk sponsored by the Theosophical Society at 3 pm tomorrow in room 401 Creative Arts Building 64 E. Van Buren St.
notable_details: Says she has used the name Peace Pilgrim for almost 30 years (15 of preparation and almost 15 of walking). Sleeps in a bed about three-fourths of the time.

route_before: Last visit to Milwaukee was in 1961
route_planned: A week's visit; schedule planned until the end of 1972
people_mentioned: Mr. and Mrs. Richard Franz (19801 W. Pinecrest La. New Berlin); Mrs. Adale S. Vaughan (2105 N. Summit Ave.)
notable_details: In Milwaukee for a week; spoke in a private home Wednesday evening; no public appearance planned. Index title lacks the place; the masthead is The Milwaukee Journal.

route_planned: Two talks: 9:30 am Wednesday assembly at Sams Chapel Kansas Wesleyan University and 4 pm student-faculty discussion at McAdams student center
notable_details: Walked into Salina Monday afternoon (Oct 30) to begin a series of Kansas speaking engagements; concentrating on the Midwest for her fourth pilgrimage. Says she lived through World War I when you might be lynched for talking about peace. Proposes that neutrals supervise nationwide elections in Vietnam.

publication: Journal and Courier (Lafayette IN; by Nancy Baker)
miles_reported: 25,000+; 5000 in 200 walking days the first year
route_before: Return visit at the invitation of Mr. and Mrs. Victor Lane; has been in Indiana three other times
route_planned: Knows day by day where she will be until year end and month by month until end of 1972; back in Indiana October 1971
people_mentioned: Mr. and Mrs. Victor Lane; Ron Hoyman (Purdue student who arranged the meeting)
notable_details: Returned to Lafayette Wednesday (Mar 27); spoke that night at a Purdue University meeting. Proposes neutral nations supervise Vietnam elections.

miles_reported: 25,000 logged by end of 1964; since completed another four-year circuit
route_before: Walked in from Winchester (spoke there earlier in the week after a woman heard her on network radio); first official visit since April 1962 (briefly in October 1965)
route_planned: Leave early next week for a talk at Portage in northwest Indiana; later southwest Michigan; back to Fort Wayne October 1971
notable_details: Walked into Fort Wayne at midday Thursday (April 4). Spoke Thursday evening at Unity Church (3200 Leroy St.); Sunday 10:30 am Unity service and 3 pm Theosophical Society meeting at the Central YMCA. Says she was inspired while viewing the countryside from a hilltop while visiting in New England.

route_before: First pilgrimage: Arizona New Mexico Texas Oklahoma Kansas Missouri Illinois then along the lake front through Gary to Michigan and across the Great Lakes states to New York
route_planned: Gary is on her schedule for October 1971
people_mentioned: A woman in Pennsylvania (keeps her schedule)
notable_details: Photographed walking a Gary sidewalk. Says thirty years ago she was by today's standards a successful woman. Describes the New England hillside vision of a US map with a jagged course from Los Angeles to New York.

publication: The Alliance Review (Alliance OH; by Charlene Billo; photo Thomas Hagan)
route_before: Arrived in Alliance Wednesday afternoon from Canton (walked through Alliance about six years earlier)
route_planned: This morning left for Youngstown (a woman who heard her on radio); then walk to Steubenville for a local television interview
people_mentioned: Mrs. Pearl Carlson (499 W. Main St.; invited her through a mutual friend in Toledo)
notable_details: Says she previously worked with the elderly and the psychologically disturbed. Has addressed all the major denominations; record seven sermons on one Sunday. Hasn't had a cold or headache for 30 years.
date_note: Hand-dated Mon May 20-68; visit Wednesday May 15 1968.

publication: The Washington Post (by Sarah Booth Conroy; photo Tom Allen)
route_before: Takes rides when convenient now that superhighways bar pedestrians
route_planned: Noon Tuesday talk at University of Maryland Student Union room 114; meetings at Howard University and George Mason College; Wednesday 7:30 pm Union Methodist Church
notable_details: Stood yesterday (Sunday Oct 27) before the congregation of Christ Congregational Church in Silver Spring. Says she knew Martin Luther King. Gave her evening dresses away years ago. Shoe size 6C.

miles_reported: 25,000 counted plus hundreds uncounted; four pilgrimages
route_planned: Fifth pilgrimage starting now: three weeks in Los Angeles then south to San Diego on the way to Florida; Sunday 11 am Conference on Science and Religion in Northridge; a week from Sunday Church of Truth Pasadena; Hayward Hotel 2:30 pm Jan 26
notable_details: Told a press conference Wednesday (Jan 8) she would skip her usual year off between pilgrimages because of the world situation. Has been picked up for vagrancy and for walking through dangerous parts of town at night.

publication: Los Angeles Times (photos by Joe Kennedy)
notable_details: Photos: walking on a railroad track (a favorite footpath) in Los Angeles.

route_before: Last cross-America hike brought her to Seattle three years ago (1966); spoke to women at the Des Moines United Methodist Church
route_planned: Walk into Seattle tomorrow (Saturday June 21); speak at Fellowship Hall of the University Congregational Church 10 am Sunday
notable_details: Photo caption: Peace Pilgrim walked in Des Moines (Washington state suburb south of Seattle). Says she began living a simple life 31 years ago. Says the first pilgrimage was hardest: faced death in a snowstorm; attacked by a maniac teenage boy; questioned in prison as a vagrant. Did not stop between the fourth and fifth pilgrimages because of Vietnam.
date_note: Hand-dated Seattle Times Washington Friday June 20 1969.

people_mentioned: Mark Henle (photographer)
notable_details: Two photos (close-up portrait; her worn canvas shoes: Shoes like this last 1500 miles). Caption says she thinks she may be able to cease her walking pilgrimages in 10 years. Date and place unknown (style suggests 1970s).

publication: Pine Bluff Commercial (by Judi Norton; photo Bill Loyd)
route_planned: Speaking schedule: today 7:30 pm Trinity Episcopal Church (703 W. Third Ave.); Sunday 9:45 am First United Methodist Church
people_mentioned: The Jim Roth family (hosts; 3909 King Richard Rd.)
notable_details: Walked into Pine Bluff yesterday (Friday Feb 26). Says the day after the 1953 Rose Parade she gave an interview to the Los Angeles Times. Says her childhood home was sold long ago. Says her preparation began in 1938. Worked with the elderly and the psychologically disturbed.

publication: The Lima News (Lima OH; by Beverly Massie)
route_before: Return visit to BLUFFTON (Ohio) after a short visit four years ago
route_planned: Leave Bluffton about 9:30 am Saturday for Findlay; Sunday morning talk at the Salem-Cass United Methodist Church; booked until 1977
notable_details: INDEX ERROR: listed as Bluffton SC - this is Bluffton OHIO (Lima News). Tells of a near-death experience in a snowstorm: after crawling into a cardboard box under a bridge she saw relatives who had crossed over.

route_before: Visited Springfield four years ago during another election year (1968; 25000 miles then)
people_mentioned: Rev. and Mrs. Robert Dick (hosts)
notable_details: Spoke to Unitarian women at the Dick home; at the Springfield library; and to young people at the parsonage in Londonderry.

publication: Buffalo paper (Religion News; probable Buffalo Evening News)
route_planned: Daily itinerary of speaking engagements set for the rest of the year
notable_details: Spoke Friday night to a small group in the dimly lit parlor of the International Institute on Delaware Ave. Says she rides some now (hitchhikes). Hopes young people will vote for peace in the coming election (1972).
Was in Princeton again last week to speak at the Quaker Meeting House.

miles_reported: 25,000 reached nine years ago (1964); not counted since
route_before: Began her sixth cross-country walk in southern California five months ago and has traveled north through the center of the state; marched into Grass Valley Saturday (May 12)
route_planned: Chico then up the coast to Oregon and Washington; then south into Nevada; a five-year pilgrimage
notable_details: Spoke at a picnic at Pioneer Park in Nevada City Sunday; Wednesday morning to students at Nevada Union High School. Says walking used to be most important; now speaking is first answering letters second and walking third.

publication: East Oregonian (Pendleton OR; by Betty Ehlers)
route_before: Sixth zig-zag trip across the country; was in Pendleton this summer
people_mentioned: Friends in Pendleton (offered new shoes)
notable_details: Profile: mail goes to a small-town post office that forwards it; she picks it up once a week. Wears a sun suit under her clothes as swimsuit or spare. Confirms the paper as the East Oregonian (Pendleton).

publication: The Statesman (Salem OR; by Leslie Zaitz)
notable_details: Brought her ambition to Salem this week for the fifth time. Says she has slept on the front seat of a fire engine a city hall conference table and a cardboard box under a railroad trestle.

publication: Seattle Post-Intelligencer (Dialogue by Earl Hansen; photo Paul Thomas)
route_planned: Here for the rest of July: classes at the University of Washington Seattle University and Seattle and Shoreline Community Colleges; University Friends Meeting Sunday 10 am; Unity Church of Truth next Wednesday 7:30 pm
notable_details: Said here yesterday (Wednesday July 18) she no longer feels like a voice crying in the wilderness. Says she received her calling while on a New England vacation in 1953 (other sources say 1952).

miles_reported: 10,400 (meter on Sunday); 12 pairs of shoes; six uniforms
route_before: Has trudged through BC Alberta and Saskatchewan averaging 100 miles in each province; walked 50 miles before Brandon then 50 to Winnipeg; slept in a parked car one night and on grass under a newspaper the next; no food from Friday noon to Sunday morning
route_planned: Public meeting Thursday 8 pm at the Unitarian church (Sargent Ave. and Banning St.); then on east
people_mentioned: A West Coast resident who asked a Winnipeg friend to set up the meeting
notable_details: Walked into the Free Press newsroom Sunday night (first time in Winnipeg). INDEX DATE WRONG: index says 1973 but the tunic reads Ten Thousand Miles on Foot for World Peace and the mileage and province sequence match summer 1957 (after Moose Jaw June 24 1957). Reporter's 200000 miles in 20 years is clearly a misprint.
date_note: Undated; a Sunday in late June or early July 1957 (June 30 or July 7).

notable_details: Photo: visiting Marin for the fifth time. Hand notes mention Pendleton and San Rafael.

publication: Los Angeles Times (Part IV p.4; continuation)
route_before: Sixth pilgrimage started in California (all six started there); spending eight months in California this time
notable_details: One morning late last week she appeared downtown for a practically predawn interview. Says she was born on a farm in New Jersey around the turn of the century and did office work for the Friends for 15 years. Says she was once picked up as a vagrant in 1953. Record: seven sermons in one Sunday.

route_planned: Sixth pilgrimage: all 48 states in 1973-77; several months in Southern California (coordinator Mary C. Eubanks 614 1/2 W. 40th Pl. Los Angeles)
people_mentioned: Lois Krenz (former school principal; host in Altadena); Mary C. Eubanks (coordinator)
notable_details: Spent two days in Pasadena and made one talk. Asked whether she would walk ahead of the Rose Parade this year (her 21st anniversary): she might. Wears 6-C children's deck shoes.

publication: Detroit Free Press (photo by Ira Rosenberg)
notable_details: Photo only: stepping out on her trek through Detroit. Date not on clipping (index says 1973).

route_before: Walked into Southern California
route_planned: Knows where she will be every day until September and every month until 1978
notable_details: Datelined Fullerton. Spoke Thursday night (Jan 17) at the Psynetics Foundation 1212 E. Lincoln Ave. Anaheim. Says she has preceded the Rose Parade six times. Permanent address care of a friend in Cologne NJ (a farming community where she has never lived). Says Peace Pilgrim has become her legal name in many states.

publication: The Register (Santa Ana CA; by Trish Huether)
route_planned: Sixth pilgrimage through all 48 states by 1977
notable_details: Spoke to the Women's Fellowship of First Presbyterian Church Fullerton. One woman Peace stayed with said Peace told her she came from a wealthy family and had a college education. Says her pilgrimage began 36 years ago (preparation from about 1938).
date_note: Hand-dated The Register Santa Ana California January 30 1974.

publication: The San Diego Union (photo George Smith) and Coronado Journal letter
route_before: Schedule solid for a month before she arrived in San Diego
route_planned: For a few days beginning Feb 10 staying in Coronado; Sunday Feb 10 7:30 pm talk in the Parish Hall of the Presbyterian Church (Tenth St. and C Ave.); many talks in San Diego
people_mentioned: Kathleen Bond (letter writer)
notable_details: Union photo: walking in Balboa Park. Says when she quit her job and gave up her home and divorced herself from material possessions the year was 1953 (wording partly cut off).
date_note: Union masthead February 9 1974; Coronado Journal letter hand-dated February 7 1974.

publication: State Press (Arizona State University Tempe; by Kevin R. Gustafson; photo Lenny Lind)
route_planned: In the Valley (Phoenix area) for the rest of the month speaking to classes and gatherings
notable_details: Spoke Wednesday afternoon (April 10) before ASU's Tolstoi-Gandhi class. Says she has been given everything she needed without asking for 25 years.

route_planned: Will speak to various classes on Phillips University campus Monday (Mar 10)
notable_details: Talked about peace Friday morning (Mar 7) at the Christian Church in Waukomis. Says thirty-seven years ago she was wealthy and unhappy.

route_before: Last in Stillwater in December 1970
route_planned: Expects to walk another 10 years; may go to Alaska and Hawaii this summer; schedule allotted through 1984; back to Stillwater in 1980; Wewoka and Tulsa next
people_mentioned: Mr. and Mrs. J. E. Robinson (hosts; 2104 Admiral Rd.; 7 pm meeting tonight)
notable_details: Back in Stillwater. Tunic now says only 25000 miles on foot for peace (dropped the word world).
Photo: sitting on a car hood showing worn canvas shoes.

route_before: Previously spoke in Winfield in 1970
route_planned: On the Southwestern College campus until Saturday; KNIC radio interview 10:30 am Thursday; KSWC FM call-in 9-10 pm Thursday and Friday
people_mentioned: Chris Hill; Clif Elder; Donnie Davison; Dr. John Paulin; David Parker (students/faculty in photo)
notable_details: Returned to Winfield and Southwestern College this week.

publication: Unknown paper (staff photos by Hugh Tessendorf)
people_mentioned: Hugh Tessendorf (photographer)
notable_details: Two photos: patched canvas shoe (they last about 1500 miles); walking a sidewalk. Caption: her journey began 21 years ago; Peace Pilgrim's making her sixth stop here. Place not identified.

route_before: Arrived in Stuart Wednesday for a few days walking from another part of the country
route_planned: This year a seventh pilgrimage to Alaska and Hawaii (the only states not yet visited) financed by a businessman: one week in Alaska and two in Hawaii
notable_details: Writing to government officials and the UN from Stuart asking for a Peace Department tied to the Bicentennial and for a world language. Says she worked with the elderly then counselled the psychologically disturbed and earned money as a typist for a few hours. Photographed during a visit to O'Neill and Holt County last week.
date_note: Masthead Thursday June 5 1975; visit late May 1975.

route_before: Walked down to Albuquerque Saturday following her stay here
route_planned: Plans to be back in Santa Fe (date misprinted as 1970)
notable_details: Says she gave up home possessions age and name in 1953. Mail through general delivery in Cologne NJ. The continuation section appears to be from a Santa Fe paper (says she walked down to Albuquerque Saturday after her stay here).

route_planned: Sixth Pilgrimage Route around the US
notable_details: Short feature with cartoon illustration. Says she counted highway markers until she reached 25000.

publication: The Edinburg Daily Review (by Dorothy Maville)
route_planned: Sunday 10:30 am Unitarian-Universalist Fellowship (Student Center for Social Involvement 1615 W. Kuhn Edinburg); Sunday 6:30 pm First United Methodist Church McAllen; leave the Valley next week for Corpus Christi then Houston
people_mentioned: Mrs. Dorothy Maville (Review Society Editor)
notable_details: Spoke on the patio outside the Student Center at Pan American University. Says in the early days she was investigated by a Congressional committee. Now speaking comes first then mail then walking.
date_note: Hand-dated The Edinburg Daily Review Edinburg Texas January 30 1976.

route_planned: Featured speaker at the Rotary Club Wednesday
notable_details: Arrived in Alice last Friday for a very temporary halt. Spent the weekend addressing Alice High School students; Sunday morning services at First United Methodist Church; radio and local TV interviews. Says she sometimes earns her keep by typing or caring for the mentally ill. Says she once came through the city of her birth and a native told her anyone would know you're not from here by the way you talk.
date_note: Undated; early 1976 (between Austin Jan 10 and Edinburg Jan 30).

publication: Chattanooga News-Free Press (by Barry Parker; photo Robin Hood)
miles_reported: 25,000 long ago exceeded; crossed the country seven times in 23 years
people_mentioned: B.J. Odom; Joyce Cooke; Howard Wright; Phyllis Haley (UTC students in photo)
notable_details: Arrived in Chattanooga Monday (Apr 26); fifth visit. Spoke earlier in the day to three classes at Brainerd High School and to a group at UTC's University Center. Says she was born poor but reached a position of affluence. Pilgrimage began in the midst of the Korean War and the McCarthy hearings.

publication: UT Daily Beacon (University of Tennessee Knoxville; by Gene Forrest; photo George Holz)
route_before: Came to Knoxville from Nashville on foot
route_planned: On her way to Kentucky on foot
notable_details: Spoke at Fort Sanders Presbyterian Church Tuesday (May 11) at the request of Epworth Ministry. Bicentennial suggestions: a peace department and a UN world language taught as a second language. Speaks to college classes in sociology psychology and philosophy.

publication: UT Daily Beacon (second copy of row 222)
notable_details: Fuller copy of the same article.

publication: Evansville paper (Morning assignment column by Joe Aaron)
route_planned: Speak tomorrow 5:30 pm at Central Library (sponsor Evansville Peace Fellowship)
notable_details: Itinerary roughly outlined into the mid-1980s. Says she was born on a farm on the outskirts of a small town. Recalls a Sunday in Wyoming when she made seven speeches. Says she was once a woman on easy street with fancy clothes and a fine apartment. Confirms Evansville INDIANA (index says IA).

route_before: Visited central Illinois last week
notable_details: Was in Springfield over two days; spoke at Sangamon State University to about 35 people. Brochures prepared by devotees in Cologne NJ. Now travels mostly by thumb by faith rather than walking.
date_note: Hand-dated Springfield Illinois June 18-24 1976; visit the week before.

notable_details: This week visited the Grand Rapids area for the third time since 1953. Says in the late 1930s she began discarding possessions money and finally her name. Is given a bed by total strangers three-quarters of the time.

route_planned: Spend one week in Detroit then walk south for the winter
notable_details: Started her special mission to Detroit Wednesday (Aug 25) by walking downtown for a few hours in the morning; will walk through gang territories this week. Sixth visit to Detroit. Says she was poor as a child then made a lot of money.

publication: The Plain Dealer (Cleveland; by Robert Dolgan; photo George Heinz)
miles_reported: 50,000 on foot (her estimate from road maps); two pairs of shoes a year
route_before: For the last 12 years has mixed hitchhiking with walking
