route_planned: Speaking itinerary made up to June 1977; five talks to church groups here this week; reachable through Unity Center Church Cleveland Heights
notable_details: In town this week; fourth visit since 1953. Says she used to give her real name in interviews but it caused confusion with mail sent to Cologne. Says she was born on a farm never married and once had fine cars apartments and clothes.
date_note: Hand-dated The Plain Dealer Cleveland Ohio October 20 1976.

notable_details: Profile describing her three lives (making money; 15 years of preparation; the pilgrimage). Says in 1953 she was jailed for vagrancy in California and investigated before being dismissed as a religious pilgrim. Continuation not in scan.
date_note: Undated; 1976 (23 years after 1953); autumn leaves in the photo.

notable_details: Photo: walking a leaf-covered sidewalk past a Victorian house.

publication: The Raleigh Times (Women of The Times p.1-B; by Lynne Wogan)
route_before: Walked into Raleigh Saturday (Feb 26); spoke at the Quaker Meeting House and the Unitarian Universalist Fellowship
route_planned: Talk tonight 7:30 at the Holy Order of MANS (602 Stacy St.)
people_mentioned: Richard and Mary Leuba (hosts; he is an assistant professor of engineering at NC State)
notable_details: Says her pilgrimage began at the Rose Bowl Parade in Pasadena Jan 1 1953: she walked the parade route and kept on walking. Sometimes sleeps on roadsides and in used car lots.

route_before: Sixth crossing of the US
route_planned: Speaking at Spindale Church of the Brethren Sunday (invited by Rev. and Mrs. Rhinehardt); then Asheville; then Burnsville; then way up into Virginia
people_mentioned: Rev. and Mrs. Rhinehardt (Spindale Church of the Brethren)
notable_details: Spoke to Central (high school) students. Says she never walks Interstates (against the law). A drunk man once threw crumpled money at her shouting give it to the church and she did.

publication: The Daily Advance (Lynchburg VA; by Margaret Chabris; Aubrey Wiley photo)
route_planned: Speak today 7:30 pm at Unity in the Seven Hills Church (4709 Myrtle St.); then north
notable_details: Has an itinerary through 1984; zig-zags the country north in spring and south in fall. Says she was born on a small farm on the outskirts of a small town; spent 15 years living on $10 a week from typing while working with senior citizens.

publication: The Montgomery Journal (Montgomery County MD; by Linda Waters)
route_before: Spent the last year on the east coast speaking answering mail and walking
route_planned: Public meeting Sunday May 15 10 am at Christ Congregational Church (9525 Colesville Rd. Silver Spring); then north from the Washington DC area
people_mentioned: Mrs. Julia B. Aiken (host in Silver Spring)
notable_details: INDEX ERROR: listed as Montgomery AL; this is The Montgomery Journal of Montgomery County MARYLAND. Says she acquired inner peace at 16 when she sought God; was reared on the golden rule in grammar school.

publication: The Boston Herald American (Michael Ryan column)
route_before: Came to Boston last week; last night spoke at the Christian Community of Boston on Commonwealth Avenue
route_planned: This morning heading west
notable_details: Says on Jan 1 1953 she walked the Tournament of Roses route shortly before the procession began and every national TV network interviewed her that day.

publication: The Christian Science Monitor (by Ruth Seymour)
route_before: Recently walked through Boston; one stop was the Boston Christian Community on Commonwealth Avenue
notable_details: Says only one person in 25 years struck her (a disturbed teenager she walked with into rugged hills during a thunderstorm). Says she began reading the Bible early in the pilgrimage because she would be asked to give sermons.
date_note: Masthead Tuesday September 20 1977 (describes the early-August Boston visit).

notable_details: Photo: speaking to an audience at a church. Retells the disturbed-boy story. Vegetarian for 35 years.

publication: The Press (Atlantic City; by Mona Moore; photo)
route_planned: Expects to visit Newfield Atlantic City and Absecon later this week
people_mentioned: Mr. and Mrs. H. Jay Dinshah (hosts)
notable_details: Spoke to a small group at the home of Mr. and Mrs. H. Jay Dinshah in Malaga on Sunday. Photo on a wooded trail. Same article as row 239.

publication: The Press (Atlantic City; p.18; by Mona Moore)
miles_reported: all 50 states; 10 provinces; parts of Mexico
route_before: Almost finished with her sixth pilgrimage
route_planned: Wednesday 7:30 pm Piney Hollow United Methodist Church (Dutch Mill Road Newfield); Thursday 7:30 pm Christian Community (2323 Atlantic Ave. Atlantic City); Sunday 9:30 11 and 7:30 at Absecon Presbyterian Church; seventh pilgrimage begins next March in California
people_mentioned: Mr. and Mrs. H. Jay Dinshah (Malaga hosts)
notable_details: Datelined Malaga. Spoke Sunday (Oct 30) at the Dinshahs' home. Says she came from a life of money and things; vegetarian; no caffeine; took her vow of simplicity 40 years ago.

publication: Unknown paper (Times photo by Jim Strickland)
notable_details: Photo walking. Says her first pilgrimage took 200 walking days averaging 25 miles. No aches or colds in 39 years (places it about 1977-78).

publication: Suncoast News (Upper Suncoast FL; by Paul Stewart)
route_planned: In the Upper Suncoast area through December: Northwest Pasco Lions Club in Hudson; Hudson United Methodist Church; short trips to Eckerd College Gainesville and Ocala; finish in Florida at the end of February then head to California for the seventh pilgrimage
notable_details: Stopped in the offices of the Suncoast Shopper & News. INDEX NOTE: listed as Sarasota FL; the paper is the Suncoast News of the Upper Suncoast (Pasco County - Hudson / New Port Richey).
Same clipping as row 241.

people_mentioned: Women's Fellowship of Mira Vista United Church of Christ
notable_details: Recently visited and spoke for more than an hour to the Women's Fellowship of Mira Vista United Church of Christ in El Cerrito. Says her spiritual growth began when she left the self-centered life at 16. Admires Gandhi.
Portrait photo with caption My walking stops when we attain outer and inner peace. Same photo as in the Raleigh Times March 1 1977 continuation (row 232) - probably from that paper.

publication: The Courier (Carlsbad CA; by Cindy Dommer)
route_before: Spent the better part of this past week in Vista and San Marcos
route_planned: Booked ahead through 1984
notable_details: Says she undertook a 45-day fast in her second year (115 to 85 pounds). Says Peace Pilgrim is her legal name. Recounts the snowstorm near-death experience and defending a young girl from a man.
Continuation of row 245.

publication: The Arizona Daily Star (Tucson; by Judith Ratliff)
route_planned: Quite a number of talks in Tucson
notable_details: On her seventh transcontinental journey. Says years ago in Tucson she addressed her first college class at a psychology professor's request. Says the pilgrimage idea came on a daily morning walk with a visual road map of the first route. Mail collected by a farm woman in Cologne NJ.
date_note: Undated; 27 years after 1953 = late 1979 or early 1980.

route_before: Second trip to Scottsdale; has already climbed Squaw Peak
route_planned: Tuesday two classes at Scottsdale Community College; next week Arizona State University and Mesa Community College; in Arizona until January
notable_details: Walking Scottsdale this week. Answered questions on Iran. Mentions Mother Teresa's Nobel Peace Prize (awarded October 1979) and Amnesty International. Three friends in Cologne NJ mail her newsletter to about 10000 subscribers. A New Jersey writer is working on a book about her.
date_note: Undated; November-December 1979 (Iran hostage crisis; Mother Teresa Nobel).

publication: Arizona Daily Sun (Flagstaff; by Jim Fossum)
route_planned: Speaking tonight at the Campus Christian Center on the Northern Arizona University campus
notable_details: Says her confrontation with death came in the Arizona high country in a blanketing snowstorm when she snuggled into a large packing box. Mentions a film offer and an inspirational tour to Hawaii. Index label North Arizona = Flagstaff (NAU).

publication: The New Mexican (Santa Fe; photo Barbaraellen Koch)
notable_details: Photo only: walking a dirt path beside a coyote fence. Caption: worker for peace on all levels.

route_before: Seventh crossing - making loops this time; last in El Paso five years ago; spoke at New Mexico State in Las Cruces this trip; spoke at one quarter of the high schools in Tucson
route_planned: Friday 7 pm Unicorn Center (1401 West Yandell); Saturday 7:30 pm Mutual Savings (Montana at Reynolds); Sunday 11 am Religious Science Center of El Paso (3330 Montana)
notable_details: Says Swarthmore College has asked for her clippings for the Swarthmore Peace Collection. With the freeway system she now walks mostly in towns.

route_before: In the Midland-Odessa area this week speaking at Odessa College and Midland College
route_planned: Big Spring then Abilene and on down through the state
notable_details: Datelined Odessa. Says she legally changed her name to Peace Pilgrim some time ago. Age somewhere near 80 (reporter).
date_note: Masthead Sunday February 3 1980. Index lists the paper as Odessa; it is the San Angelo Standard-Times.

notable_details: Addressed a group last week at Chez Coffeehouse (100 Hitt St.).
date_note: Masthead Saturday April 19 1980; talk the week before.

publication: Honolulu Advertiser (by Beverly Creamer; photo Roy Ito)
route_before: Second trip to Hawaii: led a two-week educational camping tour of 15 people around the islands
route_planned: Sunday 9:30 am Church of the Crossroads (1212 University Ave.); 10:45 Good Shepherd Lutheran Church (638 N. Kuakini St.); leaves Monday flying to Los Angeles then Bismarck ND to resume her pilgrimage
people_mentioned: Rev. William Kautz (United Church of Christ Honolulu)
notable_details: Says she was investigated during the McCarthy era. Once slept on the front seat of a fire engine in Tombstone AZ. Says she lived in Los Angeles in fine apartments before 1953. Loops through Cologne NJ every so often to visit the friend who forwards her mail.

route_before: A week in Topeka: Unity Church; Church of the Brethren; Washburn University classes
route_planned: On her way to Dallas to lecture at a Catholic convent; seventh pilgrimage will take her through the 48 states in about six years
people_mentioned: Barney Hubert (stopped to talk on US-40 east of Topeka)
notable_details: Passed through Topeka this week. Calls Cologne NJ her home base. Says she began a more austere life in the late 1930s living on about $10 weekly.

publication: Mankato Free Press (probable; John Cross photo)
notable_details: Photo: talking about individual and world peace; pockets hold a comb folding toothbrush pen and unanswered mail.

publication: Arlington Daily News (TEXAS; staff photo Olin Boese)
route_before: Current Metroplex (Dallas-Fort Worth) sojourn
route_planned: Speak this (Sunday) morning to the Unity Church of Arlington at an 11 am service at the Holiday Inn on Collins
notable_details: Photographed stepping out on Abram Street (at S. West St.). Said Friday she prays without ceasing and walks without fear; opposed to any use of nuclear power. Confirms Arlington TEXAS.
date_note: Undated; late 1980 (follows Topeka Nov 8: on her way to Dallas).

publication: New Orleans Sun (hand label; staff photo Ellis Lucia)
notable_details: Photo with headline only: Pilgrim finds inner peace by walking in harmony.

publication: The Capital Times (Madison WI; by Phil Haslanger; photo David Sandell)
route_planned: Back on the road toward Markesan Manitowoc and Milwaukee
notable_details: In Madison on her seventh pilgrimage. Sunday (June 14) spoke to the Madison Friends meeting; Tuesday afternoon (June 16) at the 4:45 pm mass at St. Paul Catholic Center on State Street. Tells of stepping in to defend an 8-year-old girl from a large man.

route_before: Several appearances at churches in Elkhart and Valparaiso this week
route_planned: En route to a Senior Citizens Luncheon at Koontz Lake
people_mentioned: Euwell Ward (70; Knox Senior Citizens Service Van driver; died 3:55 pm Tuesday); Dana McPheron (18; Rt. 2 Knox; other driver); Deputy Starke County Coroner Roger Braman
notable_details: DEATH: Mildred Norman Ryder 71 killed in a two-car head-on collision on Ind. 23 just north of Knox about noon Tuesday July 7 1981; pronounced dead at the scene. Spoke in Elkhart on Monday (July 6). Braman Funeral Home in charge.

route_before: Spoke at three services at United Methodist Church in Valparaiso Sunday (July 5)
route_planned: Was being driven to her next speaking engagement in Elkhart
people_mentioned: Euwell Ward of Bass Lake (driver); Dana McPheron of Knox; Rev. John Wolf (Valparaiso United Methodist; knew her since the late 1950s); Mrs. Eugene Young (younger sister; her Cologne NJ contact point); a brother in North Carolina
notable_details: DEATH: killed Tuesday afternoon in a crash east of Knox; the other car crossed the median on Indiana 23. Real name Mildred Norman; born July 18 1908 near Cologne NJ per the birth certificate in her pockets. Cremation then burial in New Jersey. Index said Knox TX/TN - this is Knox INDIANA.

publication: The Leader (Starke and Pulaski counties IN; photo Bob Dem...)
route_before: Came to Knox on Monday (July 6); was visiting the Ward family at the time of the accident
people_mentioned: Ewell Ward (70; Knox; Starke County Senior Citizens bus driver; Masonic Lodge member); Dana McPheron (RR 2 Knox; other driver); police officer Chat Fletcher
notable_details: DEATH: crash Tuesday afternoon on S.R. 23 north of Washington Township Elementary a half mile north of 75N. Photo of the wreckage. The other driver told police she was on the wrong side of the highway after exiting a narrow bridge and oversteered. Says she walked across the US seven times.

route_before: Had been in Elkhart at least once before (September 1976)
route_planned: Was to arrive in Elkhart July 7 and stay with Rev. Robert and Helen Dick; radio and TV appearances; speaker Monday night for the Fellowship of Reconciliation
people_mentioned: Rev. Robert Dick (Unitarian Universalist Fellowship Elkhart) and Helen Dick; Uler (Euwell) Ward
notable_details: DEATH: killed Tuesday in a two-car collision on Ind. 23 near Knox; was to arrive in Elkhart today. NOTE: contradicts row 262 which says she appeared in Elkhart on Monday. Meeting still scheduled 7 pm at City Church of the Brethren.

route_before: Visited Valparaiso last weekend at the invitation of First United Methodist Church; walked around the Courthouse Square
people_mentioned: Dr. John D. Wolf (First United Methodist minister); her sister in Cologne (forwarded her mail; arranging cremation)
notable_details: DEATH report. Photo was taken during her Valparaiso visit the weekend before. Church to hold a memorial service in the next couple of weeks.

route_before: Spoke in Chattanooga in 1971 and 1976
route_planned: Was to have been in Chattanooga Oct. 31 - Nov. 16 1981; eight states including Tennessee on her walking schedule this year; seventh pilgrimage began 1978 and was to end 1983
people_mentioned: Mary Brown Hodge (widow of Methodist Bishop Bachman Hodge; met her in Birmingham in 1956); W. Sherrill Milliken (chair of Nobel nominating committee); Larry Ingle; Sara Watson; Mike Matoin (Unity Church of Chicago)
notable_details: Friends react. A Chattanooga committee nominated her for the Nobel Peace Prize this year. A letter sent to her at Elkhart was returned stamped Deceased. Physically attacked only twice.

route_before: Spoke at two services of the Unity Church of Hammond on June 1 1981; also appeared on TV and radio in Chicago Milwaukee and Hammond
people_mentioned: Rev. Grace Free (Unity Church); Rose Iatarola (secretary)
notable_details: Memorial service today 8 pm at Unity Church of Hammond (740 River Drive). Says she spoke at more than 1200 churches and every major college.

route_before: Visited Yankton and other South Dakota towns a year ago (summer 1980); last plea for peace at First United Methodist in Valparaiso July 5
people_mentioned: Mrs. Eugene Young (sister; Cologne); a brother in North Carolina
notable_details: DEATH notice. Says she was cremated and buried in New Jersey. As her eyesight failed she accepted more rides.

publication: The Courier (Carlsbad; continuation p.17 - rotated scan)
route_before: Spent the better part of this past week in Vista and San Marcos
people_mentioned: James Skovmand (photographer)
notable_details: Continuation of row 245 (rotated scan). Says her children's sneakers last about 1500 miles a pair.

publication: The Courier (Carlsbad; photos by James Skovmand)
people_mentioned: James Skovmand (photographer)
notable_details: Three photos: walking a dirt path (tunic back); two portraits.
Retrospective: says she was born on a small farm in the East early in the century and grew from modest roots.

route_before: Once visited Hemet and San Jacinto speaking to groups
people_mentioned: Ann and John Rush (43480 Cedar Ave. Hemet; moved from Whittier where they lived 18 years)
notable_details: Posthumous: Peace Pilgrim Center opens in Hemet (world headquarters) run by Ann and John Rush. The book Peace Pilgrim: Her Life and Work in Her Own Words published a year earlier (1983); 15000 copies distributed. Says she died in summer 1981 aged 73.

publication: Los Angeles Times (by Ann Japenga; photos Jim Burton and Tony Barnard)
route_before: Passed through Kansas on her final crossing (photo)
people_mentioned: John and Ann Rush (Hemet)
notable_details: Posthumous profile of the Rushes continuing her work. Says she first set out from the Pasadena Tournament of Roses Parade in 1953 and was killed near Knox IN at 73.

route_before: In 1957 passed through British Columbia and spoke to the Rushes and four other Quaker families at Kootenai (Kootenay) Lake; the Rushes later hosted her in Whittier
people_mentioned: Helene Young (sister; 70; forwarded her mail); Jean Soderland (Swarthmore College Peace Collection curator)
notable_details: Biographical detail from her sister: captain of the debating team at Egg Harbor NJ high school; eloped with a man trying to start a trucking firm in the Depression; later divorced; after an all-night walk in the woods resolved to devote her life to service; 15 years with emotionally disturbed adults and peace groups. Vision of the pilgrimage came on a New England mountaintop after hiking the Appalachian Trail. Swarthmore holds a tunic and sneakers.
Second scan of the row 273 continuation.

route_before: The day before her death appeared on radio station WKVI in Knox IN
notable_details: Says she was killed by an inebriated driver (not stated in the 1981 reports). Ann Rush recalls her visit to their Whittier home.

publication: Enid News and Eagle (Window on the Past; by Bill Edson)
route_before: Visited Enid five times: 1955 (second pilgrimage); 1968 (fourth); 1971; 1975; and December 1980
route_planned: From Enid in December 1980 she planned: Bartlesville and Tulsa; south to Muskogee; back west to Oklahoma City Norman and Wayne; Dallas for Christmas with an order of nuns; January-March 1981 touring Texas and Louisiana; then north in spring
people_mentioned: Dr. and Mrs. Irving Smith (First United Methodist Church Enid)
notable_details: Retrospective. On her last Enid visit she attended a concert at Phillips University and spoke to church women and a sociology class. Had plans to return to Alaska and Hawaii. Index says Enid OH; it is Enid OKLAHOMA.

publication: The Desert Woman (Palm Springs; Books That Inspire by Janis M. Wolff)
notable_details: Book review of Peace Pilgrim: Her Life and Work in Her Own Words (Ocean Tree Books 1991). Says she began preparations in 1938 and later journeyed into Canada Mexico Alaska and Hawaii.
